findings.message: `o` (Orders) and `i` (order_items) are matched on `i.user_id = o.user_id`, a unique key of neither, so each row of one pairs with every matching row of the other: the result can hold more rows than both, and counts or sums over it are multiplied.
findings.fix: Match on a unique key of one side, for example add `o.order_id = i.order_id`, or reduce one side to one row per matched value with GROUP BY or DISTINCT first.
